title: The positive impact of red palm oil in school meals on vitamin A status: study in Burkina Faso
authors: Zeba AN, Martin Prével Y, Somé IT, Delisle HF
population: Primary-school pupils in Burkina Faso: 15 intervention schools in Kaya (pre-post design) and 24 schools in Bogandé randomised to usual school lunch, a single 60 mg vitamin A capsule, or 15 ml red palm oil in meals 3 times a week
funder: Micronutrient Initiative (Canada) provided most of the funding for the RPO project and for this study.
authorConflicts: The author(s) declare that they have no competing interests.
result: 15 ml of local red palm oil provided approximately 1500 µg retinol activity equivalents, based on analyses of the oil. Bogandé, serum retinol below 0.70 µmol/L at baseline and after 12 months: red palm oil 40.4% to 14.9% (n = 114); vitamin A capsule 46.1% to 17.1% (n = 117); usual lunch 23.6% to 14.2% (n = 106, p = 0.08). Mean serum retinol: red palm oil 0.82 to 0.98 µmol/L, capsule 0.77 to 0.98 µmol/L, usual lunch 0.96 to 0.94 µmol/L. Baseline serum retinol was higher in the usual-lunch group despite randomisation; endline differences between groups were not significant.
